name: Oil (Brent)
summary: Brent near $98 on 6 Nov, heading for its biggest weekly fall since 2020 on hopes of Gulf diplomacy
state: Brent settled near $98.3 on 6 Nov, down 6% in a month and inside the $85–110 Watch band (Yahoo Finance); Reuters said it was set for its biggest weekly drop since 2020 (BNN Bloomberg). Prices eased as Qatar's emir discussed ending the war with President Trump on 6 Nov, although tankers were again damaged near Hormuz on 5–6 Nov (CBS News). No physical outage above 2 mb/d was confirmed this run.
for_you: Pump prices tend to follow crude with a lag of a few weeks; they remain well above last year's levels. Describes market conditions only; it is not advice.

why: Oil feeds inflation, transport and household budgets; price spikes have preceded most post-war recessions.
drivers: OPEC+ output, Middle East supply risk, sanctions, demand, inventories, shipping disruption.

rubric.alert: Brent > $110, or 1-month change > +30%, or a major physical supply outage (> 2 mb/d).
